approach: Add `check_request_coverage(reading, request)` in a new module `crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs` (declared in reading.rs with `mod coverage;` and `pub use coverage::*;`). It is wired as ONE `step!` line, last in `refusing_check`. It parses the acceptance bullets of the request (trimmed lines under an `Acceptance` heading; a wrapped continuation line is joined to its bullet) and refuses, naming every uncovered bullet verbatim, when the union of the reading's criteria does not cover a bullet. A bullet is judged only on what is specific to it. (a) Distinctive tokens (paths, `--flags`, file names) must ALL appear in the criteria text (a path also counts when its last `/` segment appears). (b) Otherwise the bullet's specific stems are its stems minus the stems of every other bullet and of the request's non-bullet lines (fallbacks: minus other bullets only, then all stems). The bullet is covered when AT LEAST ONE specific stem is related to a stem of the criteria taken together. This answers finding 1: the default is already the lenient floor, and the producer gets a defined, ordered way to loosen further if the producer-loop replay holds. Stems are stripped when 3 or more letters remain, so name/names/naming/named match. Words that are parts of a distinctive token (changelog, md) are not stems. Exempt: a reading that declines or asks a question (a split may be proposed only as that question), and a request whose own non-bullet text affirmatively allows splitting the job (permission word + split + job-word, no negation or condition). The doc names the 2026-10-29 job, the question-only rule, the refusal-rate sentence and the 10% estimate. Tests in reading.rs, a 15-case `coverage_cases()` group in the refusal corpus, and a CHANGELOG item complete it.

decisions.choice: Judge a bullet on its distinctive tokens (all required) and, when it has none, on the stems it does not share with other bullets or non-bullet request lines; covered when at least ONE specific stem is related to a stem of the union of all criteria.
decisions.reason: Finding 1 (rev 3): the strictness is judged by the producer-loop replay (replay_is_held, replay.rs:296-298; limit = declared + REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS 5 = 15% for a declared 10%, replay.rs:161, 304-308), not by one hand-written probe, and a strict default leaves the producer no permitted move. The one-stem floor still refuses the cases that caused the 2026-10-29 rejection: near-identical sibling bullets reduce to their object words (a dropped 'numbered part' bullet shares none with a reading that has only the 'star bullet' criterion), and a path-token bullet needs its own path. Unioning criteria lets a reading split one bullet over several criteria.

rejected.option: ceil(n/2) of the specific stems as the default (previous plan)
rejected.why: Finding 1: paraphrasing readers (this job's criterion 1 against its bullet 1) would fail it, the replay of stored readings (limit 15%) could hold the work and the producer would have no permitted move.

rejected.option: All tokens OR half of all stems
rejected.why: Shared wording ('A test shows ...') lets a dropped bullet ride on its neighbours and a missing path pass on common words.

rejected.option: Require one criterion to contain all of a bullet's words
rejected.why: Refuses readings that split a bullet over two criteria, such as this job's own reading.

rejected.option: Ask a model whether each bullet is covered
rejected.why: Reading checks are deterministic and run in replay and check-reading with no agent (checks.rs doc of refusing_check).

decisions.choice: Loosen stemming: strip `'s`, `ing`, `ed`, `es`, `s` when 3 or more letters remain; related = equal, or both 3+ chars with a common prefix of at least max(3, shorter length - 1). Drop from the stems any word that is a part of a distinctive token (changelog, md from CHANGELOG.md).
decisions.reason: Finding 2: 'naming' and 'named' must meet 'names' (nam / nam / nam; the bare 'name' relates to 'nam' by prefix 3 = shorter length). Words of a file-name token are covered by the token rule, so 'change' no longer counts toward a bullet about the changelog.

rejected.why: Breaks accept / acceptance, which must relate.

decisions.choice: A non-bullet, non-blank line after a bullet inside the Acceptance section is a wrapped continuation: it is appended (one space) to the previous bullet's body, which is what is judged and quoted.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: skipping it dropped the second half's words and tokens; the approach and step 1 now agree.

rejected.why: Words and tokens in the second line of a two-line bullet are never checked and the refusal quotes half of it.

The refusal still happens at reading acceptance, before any producer run.

rejected.why: The corpus test that scans check_reading_acceptance for a direct `check_` call, and the mandatory step! name for a refusing corpus case, require a step! line.

decisions.choice: Read bullets only under an Acceptance heading (trimmed lines; `Acceptance`/`Acceptance criteria`, optional `#`, `*`, `_` marks and colon), ending at a blank line after a bullet or at a `Files:` line; no heading means the request is not checked.
decisions.reason: That is the shape of the failing request and of steward- and Hestia-made requests (steward.rs:581). is_bullet tests the raw line (topics.rs:266-272), so each line is trimmed first, as request_text_acceptance does (topics.rs:276-278).

rejected.why: Treats any list as acceptance and newly refuses readings whose requests carry background lists.

decisions.choice: The request allows a split only through a sentence of its non-bullet text with a permission word, the word split, a job-word near it and no negating or conditional word; the reading's own question exempts the reading.
decisions.reason: The failing request uses 'split' and 'follow-up' while forbidding the drop, so a keyword test would switch the check off for the very request it protects; 'in parts' and 'separate jobs' appear in unrelated sentences.

decisions.reason: Matches the other checks' shape (asserted at reading.rs:4702-4706); the reader has one correction round, so naming all avoids a second refusal.

rejected.option: Name only the first omitted bullet
rejected.why: A second refusal would follow after the one correction.

risks.risk: Finding 1: the producer-loop replay (run/mod.rs:2254, per the critic's finding; replay_is_held in replay.rs:296-298) holds the work when newly refused readings exceed the declared 10% plus 5 points = 15%. Heading requests are the usual case (steward.rs:581), and paraphrasing readers could push the rate over.
risks.mitigation: The declaration sets a 15% limit; it does not exempt this rule. The default is already the lenient floor (one related specific stem). Step 6 gives the ordered response if the loop replay newly refuses more than 15%: (1) relax the token rule from all tokens to any one token (a path still matches by its last segment); (2) widen `related` by one character of prefix tolerance (max(3, shorter - 2)). After each change keep the verbatim omitted-bullet case, the near-identical case and the path-token case refusing, and never raise the declared 10%. The tuning is judged by the replay, not by the single probe case.

risks.risk: Existing tests or fixtures with an `Acceptance:` heading and a reading whose criteria do not repeat the bullets are newly refused (hestia.rs, steward.rs, code_health.rs, cli tests with a scripted reader; the fake reader, fake.rs:311).
risks.mitigation: The check is scoped to the heading and identical text is always covered. Step 6 runs `cargo test --locked`; for any test newly refused, change the fixture's criteria to repeat the bullet (or, for a fake-reader flow, its request to carry no heading); never relax the check.

risks.risk: False refusals: a reading that paraphrases a bullet with no word in common with its specific stems, or gives a bare file name where the bullet gives a path, is refused although it covers the bullet.
risks.mitigation: A path token also matches by its last `/` segment; stems match by loosened related prefix (omit/omitted, name/naming, accept/acceptance); one related specific stem is enough; questions and declines are exempt. The refusal names the bullet and the question route, so one correction repairs it. The doc states the limits.

risks.risk: False acceptance: a dropped bullet whose specific words all occur in other criteria, or a multi-word bullet with only one specific stem met, is judged covered; 'change' in a criterion counts toward a bullet word 'changelog' that is not a file token.
risks.mitigation: Accepted by design: the target is the wholesale drop behind the 2026-10-29 rejection, including near-identical sibling bullets, which the near-identical and path-token tests and corpus cases pin. The limit is written in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The reader is not told of the rule, so the first reading of an affected job can be refused (reader prompt set has 2 tokens of headroom).
risks.mitigation: Prompts are out of scope. The refusal reaches the reader as its one correction (reading.rs:740-761) and names the bullet and the question route.

risks.risk: The verbatim request in the first corpus case could be refused first by another check, hiding the new check.
risks.mitigation: The new step is last, so an earlier refusal shows in `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` as 'refused by <other check>'. If one still refuses, step 4 rebuilds the case from the same two bullets and says so in its `source` string.

risks.risk: The id of the rejected 2026-10-29 job is in no file the planner could read (HISTORY.txt and the repository hold no record of it).
risks.mitigation: The doc names the date and the request of job 20261029-111121-fzx0 that describes it; the doc test asserts the date string and the phrase, not an id.

risks.risk: The allow-split sentence test can wrongly allow 'The parser may split lines in this job' (permission word, split, job-word, no negation).
risks.mitigation: The job-word must lie within 40 characters of `split`; sentences without one stay checked; the case is rare and errs toward accepting (no wasted run); the corpus pins the unrelated-wording case that matters.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the tests module of crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. Case A (distinct wording): request with an `Acceptance:` heading and bullets 'A reading that omits a bullet is refused naming the bullet' and 'CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased entry'; a reading with one criterion covering only the first gets Err whose text contains the second bullet verbatim and starts 'the reading was refused because'; `refusing_check` on it returns the name `check_request_coverage`. Case B (finding 1): bullets 'A test shows a star bullet is refused' and 'A test shows a numbered part is refused'; the reading's only criterion is the first bullet; Err naming the second. Case C (token): bullets 'docs/guide.md is documented' and 'docs/notes.md is documented'; the reading covers only the first; Err naming the second. Case D: for A, B and C a reading with criteria covering both (one paraphrased in A) returns Ok. Parser tests (`coverage_parser_*`): dash, star and `1.` bullets, an indented two-space bullet is found, a two-line (wrapped) bullet is one bullet whose body holds both lines and whose tokens from line 2 are required (finding 3), headings `Acceptance:`, `Acceptance criteria:`, `## Acceptance`, `**Acceptance:**`, stop at a blank line and at `Files:`, a bullet after the section is ignored, `1)` parts ignored, no heading gives nothing. Stem tests (`coverage_stems_*`): name/names/naming/named all related (finding 2), omit/omitted, accept/acceptance, cover/coverage, change not counted for a bullet whose word is CHANGELOG.md, shared stems removed, empty specific set falls back.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core request_coverage_refuses_an_omitted_bullet_and_accepts_full_coverage && cargo test -p athena-core coverage_parser && cargo test -p athena-core coverage_stems
demonstrations.observes: The omitting readings return Err naming the omitted bullet in all three shapes, including the near-identical and path-token ones; the covering readings return Ok; wrapped bullets and indented bullets are parsed; name/naming match.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step, check_reading_acceptance returns Ok for each omitting reading and the unwrap_err() panics; under the old 'tokens OR half of all stems' rule cases B and C are accepted; without the continuation join the wrapped-bullet test fails; with the 4-letter stripping floor the name/naming test fails.

Fixture `governed_reading(&["docs/guide.md"], &[criteria], &[])` (reading.rs:4527, exists). The request is a plain string argument; no double. `check_request_coverage` and its step line are added by plan steps 1 and 3.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. The same omitting reading is run against: (a) the request plus 'You may split this job into parts.' -> Ok; (a2) plus 'The work can be split into follow-ups.' -> Ok; (b) plus 'Do not split this job.' -> Err naming the bullet; (c) the text of this job's request (says 'split' and 'follow-up', allows nothing) -> Err; (d) plus 'The log is read in parts and the parser may split into tokens.' -> Err; (e) plus 'If it is large you may split this job.' -> Err; and the omitting reading with `question = Some(..)` against the unmodified request -> Ok; a declining reading (`capability` None) -> Ok.
demonstrations.observes: Only an affirmative, unnegated permission to split the job or work in the request's own text, or a question in the reading, lets a bullet be uncovered; unrelated 'in parts' or 'split into' sentences do not.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the allow-split rule (a) and (a2) are refused; without the negation guard (b) is accepted; with a bare 'split' keyword (c) is accepted; with a phrase list (d) is accepted.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_acceptance` with request strings as arguments; reading from `governed_reading(..)` (exists, reading.rs:4527) with `question` set in the question case. No double.

demonstrations.method: `coverage_cases()` in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs added to `cases()` (line 292). Each case starts from `case(..)`/`base_reading(request)` (criteria are the request's bullet lines verbatim; exist, refusal_corpus.rs:161, 230) and edits one field. 15 cases (id -> outcome, new tag): request-coverage-omitted-bullet-in-job-fzx0-request (this job's request verbatim, second criterion removed; Refuse check_request_coverage; acceptance-bullet-omitted, request-mentions-split-without-allowing); request-coverage-all-bullets-covered-in-job-fzx0-request (Accept); request-coverage-paraphrased-criteria-cover-bullets (this job's reading criteria 1 to 8 in the reading's own words against the verbatim bullets; Accept; paraphrased-criteria-cover-bullets; a leniency probe); request-coverage-near-identical-bullets-one-omitted (Refuse; near-identical-bullets-one-omitted); request-coverage-path-token-bullet-omitted (docs/guide.md vs docs/notes.md; Refuse; path-token-bullet-omitted); request-coverage-wrapped-bullet-second-line-omitted (a two-line bullet whose second line holds a path token the criteria lack; Refuse; wrapped-bullet); request-coverage-numbered-parts-one-omitted (`1.` `2.` `3.`, part 2 dropped; Refuse); request-coverage-indented-bullet-omitted (Refuse; indented-bullet); request-coverage-star-bullets-covered-by-one-merged-criterion (Accept; acceptance-bullet-covered-across-criteria); request-coverage-request-allows-split (Accept; request-allows-split); request-coverage-request-forbids-split (Refuse); request-coverage-non-permitting-split-wording (Refuse; non-permitting-split-wording); request-coverage-reading-asks-the-split-as-a-question (Accept; split-proposed-as-question); request-coverage-no-heading-not-read-today (Accept; no-acceptance-heading; known gap like `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today` :1719); request-coverage-bullet-after-the-section-is-not-acceptance (Accept; bullet-after-acceptance-section). The `1)` parts form stays with `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today` (:1719) and `(a)` parts with `lettered-paren-parts-not-read-today` (:1732); dash/star/`1.` bullets with `steward-three-dash-bullets` (:1677) plus the new cases; a request that cites a job without relying on it with `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying` (:1751) and `follow-up-on-a-job-the-reading-ignores` (:1764, refused earlier by check_prior_result_and_scope); retry complaint, crate-relative or governance path, brand word and environment variable are read as ordinary words inside bullets and covered by identical text, so existing cases keep their outcome. 13 new tags (acceptance-bullet-omitted, near-identical-bullets-one-omitted, path-token-bullet-omitted, wrapped-bullet, acceptance-bullet-covered-across-criteria, paraphrased-criteria-cover-bullets, request-allows-split, request-mentions-split-without-allowing, non-permitting-split-wording, split-proposed-as-question, no-acceptance-heading, bullet-after-acceptance-section, indented-bullet) are added to INPUT_FORMS, whose length changes from 52 to 65. Each case pins `bullets_expected` as `request_text_acceptance` counts it.

demonstrations.method: Test in reading.rs: (1) take the real Unreleased CHANGELOG item for the check (`include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")`, as sibling tests do) and the collapsed `///` doc above `pub fn check_request_coverage(` from `reading_source()`; assert `declared_percent(&normalised(..)) == Some(10)` on each (both are pub(super), reached from the reading.rs tests) and that each holds 'refuses more readings' and 'the higher refusal rate is intended'; (2) a reading that `refusing_check` accepts (returns None) against a request with no `Acceptance:` heading is refused with name `check_request_coverage` once the request has a heading and a bullet the reading omits, so the refusal rate rises by this check alone (finding 5).
demonstrations.observes: The declared share parses as 10 from the change's own changelog and doc; the same reading flips from accepted to refused by the new check.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the second half returns None and `assert_eq!(name, "check_request_coverage")` fails; without the declared sentence in the changelog item or doc the share is None.
